A design system the model reads, not a library you install

Artifact UI turns default-looking HTML artifacts into composed ones. Your agent reads this repo — tokens, primitives, blocks, templates — and ships one self-contained file that renders with the network unplugged.

Default output is the tell that no one designed it

Every model can write HTML. Almost none of it looks intentional: browser-default type, full-width paragraphs, a rainbow of one-off hexes, and a bordered box around everything. Readers can't say what's wrong — they just sense nobody cared.

Artifact UI fixes this at the source. Instead of styling each artifact from scratch, the model reads one small design system and composes from it. The same scale, the same accent, the same handling of space and corners — every run, no matter the content. Coherence stops being luck.

Three words run through everything

  • Restraint — the taste. Few type sizes, one accent, calm surfaces, generous space. When unsure, remove — polish is what you didn't add.
  • Tokens — the mechanism. Build only from var(); never a hardcoded px, hex, or one-off radius. Coherence is a side effect of everyone drinking from the same well.
  • The ladder — the structure. Primitives compose into blocks, blocks into templates. Reach for the highest rung that fits.
tokens→ primitives→ blocks→ templates→ one HTML file

The system in one glance

Every value lives in tokens/tokens.css — the usage rules ride along as comments beside each group. One build step compiles tokens + primitives into dist/artifact.css, the single paste that carries the whole system.

Color — one hue is the knob

Warm pastel, OKLCH. Swap --hue-accent and every shade re-derives. Backgrounds ladder from page to raised to sunk; never pure black or white.

Type — three sizes, weight does the work

Fluid scale via clamp(), no breakpoints. System-first stacks so nothing loads from a CDN. Hierarchy comes from weight and color, never from inventing sizes.

Heading, 650 Body at 400 — a comfortable measure, line-height 1.65, never full-width. Small and muted for meta — demoted by color, not shrunk to nothing. mono for code · tabular-nums for figures
Spacing base4px scale
Radii6 / 10 / 16 / 24
Prose measure68ch
Motion180ms, one ease

The ten components

The atoms of the system — their CSS lives in styles/base.css, their docs in one index file. Each one exists to answer a recurring question with a default, so the same data always gets the same shape.

ComponentClassUse for
Button.btn, .btn--accentActions — one accent button per view, everything else neutral.
Chip.chipTags, filters, small metadata pills; tinted only for gentle category coding.
List.listSimple label→value data — the default over boxed stat-cards.
Card.cardGrouped or media-rich content only — the last resort, never the default wrapper.
Record list.records, .recordCollections of records (users, issues, deployments) — the default over a table.
Tabletable, .numDense many-column comparison, where row/column scanning is the point.
Field.fieldA form input with its label and message; focus is always a visible ring.
Selectbox.selectA dropdown that looks identical on every browser and OS — CSS chevron, no native chrome.
Form patterns.form-row, .field--errorMulti-field layout and validation states — color plus a message, never color alone.
Callout.callout, __icon, --rowThe notice card — result, confirmation, or destructive confirm. The icon carries the type.

The through-line: several components are guardrails against a specific default-artifact tell. The list exists so metrics don't end up in boxed grids; the record list so collections don't get crammed into tables; the callout so notices carry their meaning in an icon instead of a colored panel.

Templates — whole documents, ready to fill

The top rung of the ladder: complete document types. Fixed-format docs ship as copyable HTML — copy, fill the slots, don't author layout. Semi-structured docs ship as a recipe composed from blocks. A decision tree in the index routes each request before any question is asked.

  • ərizə
    Azerbaijani petition/application to an authorityrecipient → applicant → body → signature + date
    Copyable Paper
  • Resume / CV
    1–2 page career documentcontact → summary → experience → skills → education
    Copyable Paper
  • Formal letter
    application or petition in any languagesender → recipient → subject → body → sign-off
    Copyable Paper
  • One-pager / brief
    exec summary, ~1 pageheader → sections → metrics list → optional figure
    Blocks recipe
  • Review / audit report
    PR walkthrough, code review, findingsverdict → summary → findings table → callouts
    Copyable
  • Timeline / status
    incident timeline, status page, changelogheader + status → dated entries on a rail → current state
    Copyable

Paper docs print for real. Resume, ərizə, and letter carry data-paper — a white sheet on screen instead of the cream app background — and pick up A4 sizing, white-paper neutralization, and safe page breaks from the print block automatically. Export is just the browser's "Save as PDF".

The content contract: no lorem ipsum, no padded prose, no invented metrics or credentials. Identity fills from the brand profile first, then the prompt; anything still missing is marked [DATA NEEDED] — never faked.

How your agent uses it

1 · Read the foundation

Load tokens/tokens.css for values and rules, then paste dist/artifact.css into the artifact's <style>.

2 · Compose up the ladder

Components → blocks; documents start from a template, general artifacts crib from a worked example.

3 · Ship one file

One self-contained HTML file, zero external requests — it renders with the network unplugged.

node scripts/build.mjs        # tokens + base → dist/artifact.css
node scripts/build.mjs --check  # CI gate: fails if dist is stale
node scripts/contrast.mjs       # WCAG AA gate on every color pair

Note: this page is the system describing itself — every color, gap, radius, and shadow above comes from dist/artifact.css, unedited.

What it costs in tokens

The skill is built to keep context load flat: a router plus two-level disclosure means a run reads only the files its request routes to, and the compiled dist is half the size of its sources. Figures below are approximate (bytes ÷ 4).

Every run reads

SKILL.md — router + laws~2.8k
tokens/tokens.css — values + rules~2.9k
dist/artifact.css — pasted into the artifact~2.7k

Baseline ≈ 8.4k: ~5.7k read as input, ~2.7k written out as the inlined stylesheet.

Read only when routed to

components/_index.md — all ten, one file~3.2k
a template (e.g. report.html)~1k
an example recipe (e.g. landing.md)~0.3k
a folder index (blocks/, templates/)~0.3–0.8k

A typical styled artifact lands around 9–12k tokens end to end, before the content itself.

Questions people actually ask

Does it work outside Claude?

Yes. The skill is plain markdown and CSS — GPT, Codex, Gemini, or any agent that can read files applies it the same way. Only the auto-discovery via SKILL.md frontmatter is Claude-specific; everything else is just instructions and tokens.

Why one file with zero external requests?

Claude's artifact hosting enforces a strict CSP that silently blocks CDNs, web fonts, and remote images. A page that depends on the network looks broken exactly where it's most likely to be viewed. System-first font stacks and inline SVG make the output indestructible.

Can I re-theme it?

One knob: --hue-accent. Every accent shade — solid, hover, quiet wash, text on accent — derives from that single OKLCH hue in both light and dark mode. Change one number, rebuild, and the whole system follows.

Will it fight my content?

No — it refuses to invent it. Templates carry a content contract: no lorem ipsum, no padded prose, no fabricated metrics. Missing information is marked [DATA NEEDED] instead of guessed.
